subject: FinTrust RFP: vendor role mapping and least-privilege declaration
messages:
From: FinTrust Security <security@fintrust.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFP Annex - subprocessor role mapping and least-privilege declaration

Alex,

Thanks for taking part in our vendor RFP. As part of our final security annex, we need a clear mapping of all third-party operators that will have any level of access to FinTrust customer data for EU workloads. Specifically we need: 

- A CSV mapping vendor -> role/responsibilities -> region -> exact privilege scope (read/write/admin)
- Any planned changes to operator assignments during the next 6 months (including timelines)
- Confirmation that KMS keys and key material remain controlled by Redwood (if applicable)
- Copies of current attestations (SOC 2, ISO) for any vendor with operator-level access

Please attach the completed FT-RFP-Subprocessor-Annex.xlsx and provide a point-by-point response by EOD 2026-12-06. Our procurement and security teams are copied.

Thanks,
Maya Reed
FinTrust Security
security@fintrust.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: FinTrust Security <security@fintrust.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: RFP Annex - subprocessor role mapping and least-privilege declaration

Alex, Vanessa —

Quick technical breakdown for the CSV columns FinTrust requested. I verified live config for EU region:

- CloudNode (cloudnode.io) — role: regional-node-operator
  - Privileges: node-lifecycle (create/start/stop) limited to EU cluster tags; metrics-read; kv-cache read-only; no access to model-store write paths.
  - KMS: no visibility. All encryption: customer-managed keys reside in Redwood KMS; CloudNode manages only ephemeral transport keys.
  - Evidence: CloudNode SOC 2 report referenced and internal attestation pending (will request).

- ModelStore Inc. — role: model-artifact-provisioner
  - Privileges: model ingestion (write) into model-store staging only; artifact validation hooks; cannot alter serving configurations or rollouts.
  - Evidence: SOC 2 + ISO listed.

Notes and constraints:
- Change window: if we need to reassign CloudNode operator responsibilities to an alternate operator, timeline is ~10 business days to cut-over for EU (coord with partner); hotfix/backout plan required.
- We will not grant any third party the 'admin' role on the tenant control plane. All orchestration-level admin actions are executed by Redwood SRE/Platform with audit logs forwarded to FinTrust on request.

I will ping CloudNode for an attestation and timeline (CCing them below).

- Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: CloudNode Ops <ops@cloudnode.io>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: FinTrust Security <security@fintrust.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: RFP Annex - subprocessor role mapping and least-privilege declaration

Hi Alex / team —

Thanks for the heads up and the draft. CloudNode confirms we can operate under the following constraints for FinTrust EU workloads:

- Scope: regional-node-operator restricted to EU cluster tags only. No access to model-store write endpoints.
- KMS: Redwood retains ownership and control of KMS keys; CloudNode only uses ephemeral session keys for intra-node encryption.
- Audit: We will provide weekly operation logs and a signed attestation. See attached: cloudnode-attestation.pdf
- Migration: We can support a role reassignment window starting 2027-01-10 through 2027-01-20 for any operator reallocation. We will coordinate maintenance windows to avoid SLA impact.

You can find our public compliance page here: https://cloudnode.io/compliance. I will also initiate the DocuSign attestation and copy you when it's ready.

Regards,
Rhea Patel
Head of Operations, CloudNode
ops@cloudnode.io

Subject: RE: RFP Annex - subprocessor role mapping and least-privilege declaration

Maya / FinTrust team —

Attached is our consolidated response and CSV mapping. Summary:

- CloudNode will act as "regional-node-operator" for EU clusters with read-only KV-cache access and no model-store write privileges. KMS remains controlled by Redwood; CloudNode only uses ephemeral session keys.
- ModelStore partners are limited to model ingestion into staging buckets and cannot modify serving rollouts.
- We will not grant any third party tenant-level admin privileges; all admin actions remain with Redwood Platform engineers and are auditable.
- CloudNode provided a signed attestation (attached) and a migration window (2027-01-10 -> 2027-01-20) if reassignments are required.

Next steps: please confirm acceptance of the mapping and the migration window. We will circulate the final DocuSign attestation once CloudNode returns it (link included). HubSpot record: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/HB-4729

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through the mapping.

Best,
